title: Evaluation and Synthesis
body:
Step two of [[Software Requirements Analysis]], and two activities in one name.

**Evaluation** is pulling the problem apart: take what came out of [[Problem Recognition]]
and break it into pieces, then work out which pieces matter, which are negotiable, and where
the requirements conflict with each other. Conflicts are normal and finding them here is the
whole point; two stakeholders wanting incompatible things is cheap to discover now and
expensive to discover in testing.

**Synthesis** is putting a solution back together out of those pieces: sketch the candidate
approaches, weigh them against the constraints (cost, schedule, what the existing systems
already do), and pick one. The output is a chosen shape for the system, not yet a
[[Specification]] and definitely not a [[Design]].

The pairing matters. Evaluating without synthesising leaves you with a pile of analysed
fragments and no system; synthesising without evaluating is jumping to the first solution
that came to mind, which is the failure [[Problem Recognition]] was trying to avoid one step
earlier.

Next step: [[Modeling]].
